questions.title: Lipogenesis elongates the fatty acyl chain two carbons at a time
questions.question: An 18-year-old obese woman on a high-fat, high-carbohydrate, sedentary lifestyle has developed lipogenesis and obesity. Which statement correctly describes an aspect of lipogenesis (de novo fatty acid synthesis)?

options.A: Fatty acid synthesis and esterification to glycerol occur primarily in muscle cells
options.B: The primary source of carbons for fatty acid synthesis is glycerol
options.C: NADP+ important for fatty acid synthesis is produced by the pentose phosphate pathway
options.D: The fatty acyl chain on the fatty acid synthase complex is elongated two carbons at a time
options.E: Fatty acids are synthesized from acetyl-CoA in the mitochondria

explanations.A: Incorrect. De novo fatty acid synthesis occurs mainly in the liver and adipose tissue, not primarily in muscle cells.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The carbon source for fatty acid synthesis is acetyl-CoA (delivered from the mitochondrion as citrate), not glycerol; glycerol supplies the backbone for esterification, not the acyl carbons.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The pentose phosphate pathway produces NADPH (the reduced form), not NADP+; it is NADPH that supplies the reducing power for synthesis.
explanations.D: Correct. On the fatty acid synthase complex the growing fatty acyl chain is lengthened by two carbons in each cycle, using malonyl-CoA as the two-carbon donor and losing one carbon as CO2 per addition. This continues until palmitate (16 carbons) is released. Two-carbon growth is a defining feature of the synthase mechanism.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fatty acid synthesis is cytosolic; the mitochondrion is where fatty acids are oxidised, and the acetyl-CoA that starts synthesis is first exported to the cytosol as citrate.

questions.learning_objective: State that fatty acid synthase elongates the chain two carbons per cycle.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: The fatty acyl chain on the fatty acid synthase complex is elongated two carbons at a time", p155

questions.title: NADPH for fatty acid synthesis comes from glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase
questions.question: NADPH for fatty acid synthesis is produced mainly by the action of which of the following enzymes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Acetyl-CoA carboxylase makes malonyl-CoA (the committed step of synthesis); it does not generate NADPH.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pyruvate dehydrogenase produces acetyl-CoA and NADH, not the NADPH used for fatty acid synthesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Glycerol kinase phosphorylates glycerol for triacylglycerol assembly; it generates no NADPH.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lipoprotein lipase hydrolyses circulating triacylglycerol at the capillary wall; it is unrelated to NADPH production.
explanations.E: Correct. The NADPH spent in each reductive cycle of fatty acid synthesis is supplied mainly by the pentose phosphate (hexose monophosphate) pathway, whose first and rate-limiting enzyme is glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase. The malic enzyme reaction contributes a smaller share. This is why highly lipogenic tissues have an active pentose phosphate pathway.

questions.learning_objective: Name the pentose phosphate pathway (glucose 6-phosphate dehydrogenase) as the NADPH source for lipogenesis.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Glucose 6 P dehydrogenase", p157

questions.title: De novo fatty acid synthesis occurs in the cytosol
questions.question: In what compartment does de novo fatty acid synthesis occur?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The mitochondrion is the site of fatty acid beta-oxidation; the acetyl-CoA for synthesis is exported from it as citrate.
explanations.B: Correct. De novo fatty acid synthesis takes place in the cytosol. Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA is carried out to the cytosol as citrate, released by ATP-citrate lyase, and assembled into a fatty acid on the cytosolic fatty acid synthase complex. The cytosolic location, using NADPH, contrasts with mitochondrial oxidation using NAD+ and FAD.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Peroxisomes carry out a specialised beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, not de novo synthesis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The endoplasmic reticulum handles fatty acid elongation beyond C16 and desaturation, not the primary de novo synthesis of palmitate.

questions.learning_objective: State that de novo fatty acid synthesis is cytosolic.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Cytosol", p158

questions.title: The skin is innervated exclusively by the sympathetic division
questions.question: Which of the following organs gets its autonomic innervation exclusively from the sympathetic division?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The heart receives a dual supply: sympathetic (accelerator) and parasympathetic (vagal, decelerator) fibres.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The penis has both supplies -- parasympathetic (erection) and sympathetic (ejaculation).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The eye has both: sympathetic (pupillary dilatation) and parasympathetic (pupillary constriction, accommodation).
explanations.D: Correct. The skin and its appendages -- sweat glands, arrector pili muscles and the great majority of cutaneous blood vessels -- receive a sympathetic supply only, with no parasympathetic input. This is one of the small set of structures that escape the usual dual autonomic pattern. The adrenal medulla is another sympathetic-only structure.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The lungs/bronchi receive both sympathetic (bronchodilator) and parasympathetic (vagal, bronchoconstrictor) fibres.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the skin as a sympathetic-only structure.
questions.subject: neuro

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Skin", p160

questions.title: The lacrimal gland is supplied by the parasympathetic division
questions.question: Which of the following organs gets its autonomic innervation exclusively from the parasympathetic division?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ventricle (heart) has a dual autonomic supply.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The heart receives both sympathetic and parasympathetic (vagal) innervation.
explanations.C: Correct. Among the options, the lacrimal gland is the structure whose autonomic control is dominated by the parasympathetic secretomotor supply, making it the mirror-image answer to the sympathetic-only skin. Most viscera receive both divisions, so the exam point is recognising the few glands driven mainly by one. Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres reach it via the cranial-nerve relay to the head.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pupil has both: parasympathetic constrictor and sympathetic dilator supply.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The penis has both parasympathetic (erection) and sympathetic (ejaculation) supply.

questions.subject: neuro

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Lacrimal gland", p162

questions.title: Choline does not enter prostaglandin synthesis
questions.question: Choline enters into the synthesis of all the following, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a choline product). Choline is acetylated to acetylcholine, the transmitter of the parasympathetic system and the neuromuscular junction.
explanations.B: Correct. Prostaglandins are the exception: they are twenty-carbon eicosanoids synthesised from arachidonic acid, a polyunsaturated fatty acid released from membrane phospholipids, not from choline. Choline supplies acetylcholine and the choline-containing phospholipids, but it is not a precursor of the prostaglandins. This is the intended exclusion on the list.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a choline product). Plasmalogens include choline plasmalogens, which incorporate choline.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS a choline product). Sphingomyelin is a choline-containing sphingophospholipid.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise prostaglandins (from arachidonic acid) as not a choline derivative.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Prostaglandins", p178

questions.title: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase
questions.question: Methotrexate is a potent anticancer agent that starves dividing cells of deoxyribonucleotides through direct inhibition of which of the following enzymes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Thymidylate synthase is the target of fluorouracil (via FdUMP), not of methotrexate.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Xanthine oxidase is inhibited by allopurinol in gout, not by methotrexate.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II is a pyrimidine-synthesis enzyme, not the target of methotrexate.
explanations.D: Correct. Methotrexate is a folate analogue that competitively and potently inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, the enzyme regenerating tetrahydrofolate. The collapsed one-carbon folate pool halts thymidylate and purine synthesis, so dividing cells cannot make DNA. This is why it starves rapidly dividing cells of deoxyribonucleotides.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Ribonucleotide reductase (target of hydroxyurea) reduces ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides; it is not the methotrexate target.

questions.learning_objective: Name dihydrofolate reductase as methotrexate's target.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Dihydrofolate reductase", p191

questions.title: Synthetic nucleotide analogues are used to treat cancer
questions.question: Synthetic analogs of nucleotides are used in the treatment of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diabetes mellitus is managed with insulin and oral hypoglycaemics, not nucleotide analogues.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Atherosclerosis is treated by lipid-lowering agents and lifestyle measures, not nucleotide analogues.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hypertension is treated with antihypertensive drug classes, not nucleotide analogues.
explanations.D: Correct. Synthetic nucleotide and base analogues (such as fluorouracil, mercaptopurine and cytarabine) are antimetabolites used chiefly to treat cancer, because they are mistaken for real nucleotides and derail nucleic-acid synthesis in fast-dividing cells. Related analogues (for example acyclovir) are used as antivirals. Their action targets the nucleotide supply that dividing cells depend on.

questions.learning_objective: State that nucleotide analogues are anticancer (and antiviral) drugs.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Cancer", p197

questions.title: Orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) is treated with uridine
questions.question: An 11-year-old girl is lethargic, weak and anaemic, with low height and weight for age. Her urine contains elevated orotic acid and uridine monophosphate synthase activity is low. Administration of which of the following is most likely to relieve her symptoms?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Thymidine alone does not refill the full pyrimidine pool needed and is not the standard treatment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hypoxanthine is a purine base and does not correct a pyrimidine-synthesis block.
explanations.C: Correct. The picture is hereditary orotic aciduria: a UMP synthase defect blocks pyrimidine synthesis, so orotic acid accumulates and spills into urine while the child cannot make pyrimidines, giving megaloblastic anaemia and failure to thrive. Oral uridine bypasses the block and refills the pyrimidine nucleotide pool, relieving the symptoms. It is the specific treatment.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adenine is a purine base and does not address the pyrimidine deficiency.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Guanine is a purine base and cannot correct the pyrimidine-synthesis defect.

questions.learning_objective: Identify orotic aciduria as a UMP synthase defect treated with uridine.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Uridine", p194

questions.title: Carbamoyl phosphate is not shared with purine synthesis
questions.question: Each of the following compounds is used in the biosynthesis of BOTH purine and pyrimidine nucleotides, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS shared). Tetrahydrofolate one-carbon units are used in both purine ring assembly and thymidylate synthesis.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS shared). PRPP donates the ribose-5-phosphate in both purine and pyrimidine nucleotide formation.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS shared). Aspartate contributes nitrogen to both purine and pyrimidine synthesis.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS shared). Glutamine is a nitrogen donor in both pathways.
explanations.E: Correct. Carbamoyl phosphate is the exception: the cytosolic form (from carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II) feeds pyrimidine ring assembly specifically and is not used to build the purine ring. PRPP, aspartate, glutamine and tetrahydrofolate are all shared, but carbamoyl phosphate is pyrimidine-characteristic. Hence it is the correct exclusion.

questions.learning_objective: Name carbamoyl phosphate as the pyrimidine-specific (non-shared) precursor.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Carbamoyle phosphate", p195

questions.title: Sickle cell anaemia is not a mitochondrial DNA disorder
questions.question: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA result in all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.A: Defects in enzymes of respiratory chain complexes I and IV
options.C: A maternal pattern of disease transmission

explanations.A: Incorrect (this IS a consequence). Mitochondrial DNA encodes subunits of respiratory-chain complexes, so its mutations impair oxidative phosphorylation.
explanations.B: Correct. Sickle cell anaemia is the exception: it is caused by a point mutation in the nuclear beta-globin gene and follows ordinary autosomal (Mendelian) inheritance, so it is not a consequence of mitochondrial DNA mutation. Mitochondrial DNA disorders instead show maternal, non-Mendelian inheritance and hit the respiratory chain. This makes sickle cell anaemia the correct exclusion.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this IS true). Because mitochondria are inherited from the ovum, mitochondrial diseases show a maternal transmission pattern.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this IS true). Mitochondrial inheritance is non-Mendelian, reflecting the cytoplasmic, maternally transmitted genome.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish nuclear-gene Mendelian disorders (sickle cell) from mtDNA disease.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Sickle cell anemia", p198

questions.title: Unwinding proteins act in the first step of DNA replication
questions.question: In DNA replication, the enzyme/protein required in the FIRST step is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. DNA ligase acts at the end, sealing nicks between Okazaki fragments, not at the start.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A DNA polymerase extends an existing primed strand; it cannot act until the helix is opened and a primer is laid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. DNA polymerase synthesises new strands after unwinding and priming; it is not the first-step protein.
explanations.D: Correct. Replication begins by opening the double helix: unwinding proteins (helicase, with single-strand binding proteins, and topoisomerase relieving supercoiling ahead of the fork) separate the parental strands so they can serve as templates. Only after unwinding can priming and DNA synthesis follow. Unwinding is therefore the first step.

questions.learning_objective: State that unwinding is the first step of DNA replication.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Unwinding proteins", p201

questions.title: RNA primer formation precedes DNA replication
questions.question: Formation of the RNA primer:

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primer is laid down before, not after, DNA synthesis at the fork.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Primer formation is a step of DNA replication, not something defined relative to transcription.
explanations.C: Correct. Because DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to an existing 3'-hydroxyl end, a short RNA primer must be synthesised by primase before DNA synthesis can begin. Primer formation therefore precedes replication (DNA synthesis) at each origin and on each Okazaki fragment. The primers are later removed and replaced with DNA.
explanations.D: Incorrect. RNA primer formation belongs to replication and is not defined as following transcription.

questions.learning_objective: State that RNA primer formation precedes DNA synthesis.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Precedes replication", p204

questions.title: Eukaryotic DNA replication is catalysed by DNA polymerase delta
questions.question: Replication of DNA in eukaryotes is catalysed mainly by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. DNA polymerase beta functions in base-excision repair, not in bulk replication.
explanations.B: Correct. In eukaryotes the bulk of new DNA on the leading and lagging strands is synthesised by DNA polymerase delta (with polymerase epsilon, and polymerase alpha laying the initial primer). It is the principal eukaryotic replicative enzyme. This distinguishes it from the bacterial replicative enzyme.
explanations.C: Incorrect. DNA polymerase III is the bacterial (prokaryotic) replicative enzyme, not the eukaryotic one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. DNA polymerase alpha lays the RNA-DNA primer but does not carry out the bulk of replication; that is polymerase delta.

questions.learning_objective: Name DNA polymerase delta as the main eukaryotic replicative enzyme.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: DNA polymerase 6 [delta]", p207

questions.title: An RNA primer is needed because DNA polymerase extends an existing strand
questions.question: Why is an RNA primer necessary for DNA replication?

options.A: The RNA primer creates the 5' and 3' ends of the strand
options.B: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to an existing strand
options.C: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to RNA molecules
options.D: The RNA primer is necessary for the activity of DNA ligase

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primer does not create both ends of the strand; it provides the initial 3' end for extension.
explanations.B: Correct. DNA polymerase cannot start a chain de novo -- it can only add nucleotides to the free 3'-hydroxyl of an already existing strand. The short RNA primer, made by primase, supplies exactly that 3' end so polymerase can begin. This is the specific reason a primer is required at each start point.
explanations.C: Incorrect. DNA polymerase extends DNA or the RNA primer's 3' end, but the reason a primer is needed is the need for an existing 3' end, not a requirement to work only on RNA.
explanations.D: Incorrect. DNA ligase seals nicks after synthesis; the primer's necessity is about giving polymerase a 3' end to extend, not about ligase activity.

questions.learning_objective: Explain the RNA primer as the 3' end that DNA polymerase extends.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to an existing strand", p208

questions.title: RNA is susceptible to alkaline hydrolysis via the ribose 2'-OH
questions.question: Which of the following characteristics distinguishes most RNA molecules from DNA?

options.A: A terminal triphosphate on newly synthesized strands
options.B: A purine or pyrimidine base linked to a pentose sugar
options.C: A 3'-phosphate group linked to a pentose sugar
options.D: A 5'-phosphate group linked to a pentose sugar
options.E: Susceptibility to alkaline hydrolysis because of neighbouring pentose hydroxyl groups

explanations.A: Incorrect. A 5'-triphosphate on a nascent strand is not a distinguishing feature of RNA versus DNA in this sense.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A base linked to a pentose sugar (a nucleoside/nucleotide) is common to both RNA and DNA, so it does not distinguish them.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A 3'-phosphate linked to a pentose is not the distinguishing feature being tested.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A 5'-phosphate linked to a pentose is common to both nucleic acids and does not distinguish RNA.
explanations.E: Correct. RNA is built on ribose, which carries a 2'-hydroxyl group absent from DNA's deoxyribose. Under alkali the 2'-OH attacks the neighbouring phosphodiester bond and cleaves the chain, so RNA is susceptible to alkaline hydrolysis while DNA is not. This 2'-OH lability is a defining chemical difference distinguishing most RNA from DNA.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute RNA's alkaline lability to the ribose 2'-hydroxyl group.
questions.subject: fnd

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: Susceptibility to alkaline hydrolysis because of neighboring pentose hydroxyl groups", p210
